group: Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk
question:
Patient note:
A 72-year-old man was evaluated late this morning in the pre-anesthetic assessment suite five days before a planned outpatient laparoscopic repair of a symptomatic right inguinal hernia that has intermittently incarcerated and limited his ability to mow the lawn or carry gardening tools; the surgical team anticipates three small trocar sites, an estimated blood loss well under 100 mL, and discharge later the same day if pain is controlled and voiding is adequate. He arrived unaccompanied after parking on the fourth level of the garage and described walking the two indoor ramps to the clinic without stopping and without shortness of breath, although he deliberately avoided straining because of groin discomfort. When asked about daily activity, he reported climbing a full flight of stairs to his workshop several times a day, pushing a light snowblower during the recent storm, and comfortably walking his dog for twenty minutes at a steady pace; he denied orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, lower-extremity swelling, or unexplained weight gain. Twelve years ago he experienced crushing substernal pressure while shoveling snow and was transported to a community hospital where an inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction was identified; emergent coronary angiography revealed a thrombotic occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery that was treated with a drug-eluting stent. He completed cardiac rehabilitation, remains on aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, and his internist recently tapered metoprolol succinate to 25 mg daily because resting heart rates had been in the low 50s. He reports no recurrent angina, no nitrate prescriptions, no coronary bypass surgery, and a nuclear stress test performed eighteen months ago for atypical left shoulder discomfort showed good exercise tolerance to eight metabolic equivalents without ischemia. Hypertension was first noted in his mid-fifties and is now controlled with losartan 50 mg each morning; fasting lipid panel last month revealed LDL 76 mg/dL and triglycerides 118 mg/dL. He has never been told he has diabetes, chronic lung disease, stroke, carotid disease, heart failure, or peripheral arterial claudication. Surgical history is limited to an open appendectomy during military service without cardiopulmonary complications. He quit cigarette smoking 22 years ago after a 25-pack-year exposure, drinks one can of light beer with weekend dinner, and denies recreational drug use. Family history includes a father who died of myocardial infarction at 81 and a sister who underwent breast cancer surgery, but there are no early cardiovascular deaths. Review of systems today is negative for palpitations, dizziness, syncope, fever, chills, night sweats, abdominal pain beyond the hernia site, gastrointestinal bleeding, or urinary symptoms. After five minutes seated, vital signs in the right arm were blood pressure 124/68 mm Hg, regular pulse 64 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98 % on room air, temperature 36.6 °C, height 178 cm, weight 82 kg, and body mass index 25.9 kg/m². He appeared well nourished and in no acute distress. Neck examination showed no jugular venous distension or carotid bruit. The point of maximal impulse was nondisplaced, and auscultation revealed a crisp S1 and S2 with no gallop, rub, or murmur. Lungs were clear to percussion and auscultation throughout. Abdomen was soft with a palpable reducible right inguinal bulge but no tenderness, rebound, or organomegaly. Distal pulses were 2+ and symmetric without edema or skin discoloration. Neurologic screening demonstrated full orientation, intact cranial nerves, 5/5 strength in all muscle groups, normal sensation to light touch and vibration, and a steady tandem gait. Pre-operative laboratory studies drawn one hour before the visit showed hemoglobin 14.1 g/dL, hematocrit 41 %, white blood cell count 6.2 × 10⁹/L, platelet count 238 × 10⁹/L, sodium 139 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, chloride 103 mmol/L, bicarbonate 24 mmol/L, blood urea nitrogen 19 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 1.17 mg/dL, corresponding to an estimated glomerular filtration rate of approximately 66 mL/min/1.73 m²; fasting plasma glucose measured concurrently was 102 mg/dL, alanine aminotransferase 22 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase 20 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 78 U/L, and international normalized ratio 1.0. A twelve-lead electrocardiogram obtained in the clinic revealed normal sinus rhythm at 62 beats/min, prior inferior Q waves consistent with the remote infarct, and no acute ST-segment deviations when compared with a tracing from last year. Upright posteroanterior chest radiograph displayed clear lung fields and a normal cardiomediastinal silhouette. Airway evaluation by anesthesia documented Mallampati class I view, inter-incisor distance 4 cm, thyromental distance 7 cm, and full cervical extension. The peri-operative plan is to continue beta-blocker, angiotensin receptor blocker, and statin on the morning of surgery, withhold solid food after midnight but allow clear liquids up to two hours pre-arrival, employ balanced general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, and use multimodal analgesia to minimize opioids. Sequential compression devices and early ambulation will be instituted post-procedure, and he has been provided instructions regarding signs of wound infection, urinary retention, or recurrent pain requiring evaluation. After all questions were addressed, he verbalized understanding of medication timing, fasting instructions, and postoperative expectations and expressed confidence in proceeding with definitive hernia repair.

Question: What is the patient's score of the Revised Cardiac Risk Index for Pre-Operative Risk? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) assigns 1 point for each of six preoperative criteria:
- High-risk surgery: the planned outpatient inguinal hernia repair is not identified as a high-risk procedure → 0.
- Ischemic heart disease: prior inferior STEMI treated with a coronary stent counts despite the absence of current angina → 1.
- Heart failure: no history or clinical findings → 0.
- Cerebrovascular disease: no prior stroke or TIA documented → 0.
- Diabetes treated with insulin: no diabetes or insulin use → 0.
- Serum creatinine >2.0 mg/dL: preoperative creatinine 1.17 mg/dL → 0.
Sum: 0 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 1.
Final answer: 1
